item.stem:
Tickets for a concert cost either 10 zeds, 15 zeds, or 30 zeds.

What FRACTION of the tickets sold for 10 zeds each?

Answer: ____

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The total cost of the journey for all the students must be 500 zeds or less.
There are 30 students in the class.

Here are the costs for visiting each town:

| Visiting Acton or Camford | Visiting Burley or Darley |
| --- | --- |
| Student Rate | Student Rate |
| Round-trip ticket: 25 zeds | Round-trip ticket: 20 zeds |
| 1/3 off for groups of 25 or more students | 10% off for groups of 15 or more students |

Which towns can they afford to visit? Show your work.

descriptors: Show costs of 500 zeds for Acton and Camford; 540 zeds for Burley and Darley; Indicates Acton and Camford
Shows 500 zeds for Acton and Camford; 540 zeds for Burley and Darley; does not indicate Acton and Camford
Finds correct cost for visiting Acton and Camford (500 zeds) or Burley and Darley (540 zeds) but not both
Indicates Acton and Camford but no calculations or incorrect calculations shown
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

A horizontal bar graph with a horizontal axis labeled "Number of Tickets". The horizontal axis is marked from 0 to 60 with tick marks every 5 units and numbers at multiples of 10: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. Four horizontal bars correspond to four people:
- Kate: bar extends to 50 (shaded black)
- Ron: bar extends to 30 (shaded light gray)
- Ruth: bar extends to 20 (shaded medium gray)
- Pete: bar extends to 40 (shaded dark gray)

reference_items.stem:
A book publisher sent 140 copies of a certain book to a bookstore. The publisher packed the books in two types of boxes. One type of box held 8 copies of the book, and the other type of box held 12 copies of the book. The boxes were all full, and there were equal numbers of both types of boxes.

b) What fraction of the books sent to the bookstore were packed in the smaller boxes?

Answer: ____

Any integer

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
